title: runtime/scheduler: adjust default batching heuristics for mixed prompt-length workloads
author: Lena Fischer
description:
Context: Baseline Run 1 showed a tail-latency regression in representative mixed prompt-length traffic shapes (short chat mixed with periodic long-context requests). The root cause was the current default batching heuristic over-prioritizing prefill packing by token count, which frequently created prefill-heavy batches that starved decode and increased queue wait for short requests (especially under concurrency ramps + streaming). This PR changes the default batching heuristic to be mixed-length aware and reduces head-of-line blocking without materially reducing throughput.

What changes: (1) Introduce prompt-length bucketing for batch assembly (short/medium/long buckets based on prompt_tokens) and bias selection toward keeping short requests flowing; (2) Add a hard cap on total prefill tokens per batch (prefill_token_budget) with a separate cap for max long-prefill members per batch; (3) Add a small decode reservation (decode_min_slots) so decode doesn’t collapse during prefill-heavy bursts; (4) Improve the heuristic tie-breaker to prefer batches with lower prompt length variance when queue depth is high; (5) Expose new knobs under scheduler config with safe defaults, and add logging/metrics tags to confirm which heuristic path is active during baselines.

Default behavior: Enabled by default for Hosted + Dedicated in the runtime scheduler config (can be overridden). For Private/on-prem, default remains unchanged unless explicitly set (to reduce surprise across customer-tuned deployments).

Before/after results (baseline harness, A100-80GB, us-east-1, runtime @ 3c9f2b1; numbers are median across 7 trials; p99 shown for tail impact):
- Shape: mixed_short_long_streaming (p50 prompt=128, p95 prompt=4k; streaming; concurrency ramp 16->96)
  - TTFT p95: 1.42s -> 1.08s (-23.9%)
  - TTFT p99: 2.31s -> 1.62s (-29.9%)
  - TPOT p95: 34ms -> 33ms (-2.9%)
  - E2E p99: 9.8s -> 7.3s (-25.5%)
  - Throughput (tok/s): 100% -> 98% (within variance budget)
- Shape: mixed_short_long_nonstreaming (same prompt mix; output=256; concurrency=64 steady)
  - E2E p95: 4.9s -> 4.1s (-16.3%)
  - E2E p99: 7.6s -> 6.4s (-15.8%)
  - Throughput (req/s): 100% -> 99% (within variance budget)
- Shape: bursty_short_chat (prompt=128; output=128; burst 0->128)
  - TTFT p99: 820ms -> 770ms (-6.1%)
  - No measurable throughput change

Notes on variance: p99 TTFT improvements are consistent across regions we tested (us-east-1, eu-west-1) once fleet driver pinning is applied; see rollout plan below for additional canary coverage.

Risk/rollout: Heuristic changes can shift utilization patterns; this PR keeps the previous path available via config (scheduler.batching.heuristic=mixed_length_v1). We also add counters to validate batch composition (prefill_token_budget_hits, long_bucket_defer_count) during canary. Release Engineering requested a staged rollout (warn-only perf gate first) aligned with the baseline gating plan.

Related: ENG-4831 anomaly triage, perf suite traffic shapes in ENG-4822, variance budgets in ENG-4826.
commits: runtime/scheduler: add mixed-length bucketing + prefill token budget
runtime/scheduler: reserve decode slots under prefill pressure
runtime/metrics: emit batch composition + heuristic path counters
config: new scheduler defaults for hosted/dedicated; preserve private default
bench: add notes for mixed prompt-length shape interpretation
conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): The approach makes sense, but I’m worried about throughput loss when the queue is dominated by long prompts. Can you clarify how decode_min_slots interacts with backpressure? Also please add a guard so we don’t over-defer long bucket indefinitely.

Lena Fischer (author): Good call. decode_min_slots is only enforced when there is decode work available; it won’t steal capacity if decode queue is empty. I added a starvation guard: if long bucket head has waited > long_starvation_ms (default 250ms), we allow it to bypass the long-per-batch cap. Also added a metric long_bucket_starvation_bypass_count so we can observe it during canary.

Noah Patel (review): Two nits + one blocker: (1) please document the new default behavior difference between hosted/dedicated vs private; (2) rename prefill_token_budget to prefill_tokens_budget for consistency; (3) blocker: the tie-breaker currently uses prompt token variance but it’s O(n) per candidate batch build; please cache or compute incrementally.

Lena Fischer (author): Addressed. Docs updated with a ‘Defaults by deployment mode’ section. Kept the name prefill_token_budget to match existing config naming (max_prefill_tokens) but added an alias prefill_tokens_budget for backward compatibility in our config loader (deprecate alias in a follow-up). For variance, switched to incremental Welford stats tracked during candidate assembly so we’re not scanning members repeatedly.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Love the tail improvements. Did you check impact on KV cache compaction / eviction rates? Mixed workloads can get weird when long prompts consume cache pages.

Lena Fischer (author): Ran with cache telemetry enabled; no meaningful change in eviction rate on the mixed shapes (within 3% relative). Added a note in tools/perf/notes and a TODO to re-check once per-request cache state annotations from PR-24077 land (so we can correlate cache state with TTFT tails more cleanly).

Sean Gallagher (review): From SRE perspective: please add a log line that prints the heuristic name + budgets at scheduler init, and ensure metrics don’t explode cardinality. We need to be able to debug nightly baseline diffs quickly without digging through configs.

Lena Fischer (author): Added a single init log with heuristic + numeric budgets. Metrics are counters/gauges without per-tenant labels (only route/model as today); no new high-cardinality dimensions. Also added a short section to runtime/docs/scheduler/batching.md about which metrics to look at when tail latency shifts.
Sofia Ivanova (approval): Approved. Please follow up with a small perf note in the baseline overview once this is deployed so folks know the baseline moved for mixed prompt-length shapes.
Noah Patel (approval): Approved with the incremental variance fix. Thanks for including the before/after baseline numbers in the PR body.
rollout_notes: Rollout plan: (1) Land behind config default for hosted/dedicated only; private remains unchanged. (2) Enable in perf-canary nightly for the mixed_short_long_* traffic shapes and watch: TTFT p95/p99, queue_wait_p99, prefill_token_budget_hits, long_bucket_starvation_bypass_count, and overall tok/s. (3) Stage to 10% hosted traffic in us-east-1, then 50%, then 100% over 72 hours if no regressions beyond variance budget. (4) Dedicated: opt-in for two internal dogfood clusters first; then roll by region with rollback = set heuristic=mixed_length_v1. (5) Baseline refresh: if this becomes the new default for release qualification, run a baseline suite re-lock per ENG-4831 follow-up and update the Q1 2026 baseline artifacts tag.
release_notes: Internal: Scheduler defaults now handle mixed prompt-length queues better; improves TTFT/E2E tail latency on representative mixed short/long workloads with negligible throughput impact. Config knobs: scheduler.batching.heuristic=mixed_length_v2, scheduler.batching.prefill_token_budget, scheduler.batching.decode_min_slots, scheduler.batching.long_starvation_ms.
